item.title: [ 37] China Crushed By Trump's Tariffs!
item.description:
China’s trade surplus tops $1 trillion as exports surge

https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/china-says-2026-trade-surplus-surpassed-1-tn-in-october-229211

China’s trade surplus reached $1.04 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026 as global investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure supported exports of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand.

Exports rose 35.2 percent year-on-year in U.S. dollar terms in October, customs data showed on Nov. 10. Growth eased from September’s 36.3 percent but exceeded the 33.5 percent forecast in a Reuters poll.

Imports climbed 41.6 percent, accelerating from 31 percent in September and beating expectations of a 32 percent rise. The monthly trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion from $133.5 billion.

China passed the $1 trillion surplus threshold for a second consecutive year, reaching it a month earlier than in 2025 and putting it on course to exceed last year’s record of nearly $1.2 trillion.

The export gains have supported an economy facing subdued consumption and a prolonged property downturn that has weakened household wealth and confidence.

The imbalance is also evident in the car market. Passenger vehicle exports rose 68.2 percent year-on-year in October, while domestic sales fell 27.3 percent, according to the China Passenger Car Association.

Weak demand at home has pushed automakers to seek more buyers overseas.

The growing surplus could increase pressure for further trade restrictions, particularly in the European Union.

Beijing and Brussels have agreed to limit Chinese hybrid-vehicle exports to the bloc, but the measures have yet to take effect. Manufacturers are expected to bring shipments forward, supporting exports in the near term.

item.title: [ 99] Trump Admits He Was Wrong About His Own Policy
item.description:
Trump says deportations were ‘too tough’ and hurt him during the midterms

https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-says-deportations-tough-hurt-midterms-rcna608208

The president said in an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he would like to work out a deal with Democrats on immigration.

President Donald Trump conceded that his immigration policies were “too tough,” saying in an interview on CBS’ “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday that mass deportations hurt him during the midterm elections.

Trump said his policies had been overly harsh in removing undocumented immigrants who hadn’t committed crimes.

“I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally,” Trump said in the interview, which was recorded Friday.

He added that “a large group of people” think immigrants who are “good people, working in a landscaping company or working in a hotel or doing something ... and, in some cases, paying taxes,” should be “allowed to stay.”

Trump pointed to immigration as one of the areas in which he wanted to work with Democrats, saying yes when he was asked whether a deal could look like the creation of legal status for undocumented workers.

item.title: [126] /out/ings with a Pipe Autumn Edition
item.description:
Last thread >>2868475

This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent
an evening by the campfire with a pipe silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>how to get started
Purchase a corn cob pipe (or a cheap briar pipe) and a pouch of Half and Half or Captain Black tobacco from a smoke shop
or online. You will need a lighter or match, and something to tamp it with--a large nail works well if you don't have a pipe tool.
Fill the pipe with tobacco, pack it down halfway, top it off, pack it down to 3/4, top it off again, pack gently and enjoy. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the tobacco tastes best when it is burning cool. Tamp and re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you.
>smoking a pipe will give you cancer
Originally the Surgeon General found that pipe and cigar smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when
most adults smoked, so they had a good sample size), had insignificant death rate increases. Nowadays, tobacco is being
legislated against while hard drugs are being legalized. Put two and two together. Tobacco is just another good thing under attack by the government.

>muh weed
Not the time or place. Start your own thread.

All tobacco users welcome.

Fill in the countries and subdivisions you have visited, talk about your map and ask others about their maps. You can use the map however you like, the colors are more like suggestions, you don't have to use them, and you don't have to use all of them. You can add or remove colors and change the map as much as you want in any way you want. Don't like this map? Upload a completely different one. Up to you. Despite what some might say, there's no "wrong" way to use the map, and new posters and less travelled people are welcome and encouraged to stay and post :) This map is a group effort by our board, and we can only improve it if people reach out to share suggestions or corrections.

This is the newest edition of the map, edition 4.0.5, updated for September 2025. Thanks to an Anon in previous threads, it is now easier than ever to fill in the map. You can use the website splored.com to easily color in entire countries with a single click.
